text:
incident-bot: Pager P1 — multigpu_comm_critical on cg-prod-3. First seen 1767108888. Symptoms: NCCL collective hang during TP4 training jobs; containers reporting CUDA Xid 79, repeated OOMs, and container crashes. Auto-bridge created: <https://meet/bridge/1767108888>

maria (infra): I'm oncall, joining bridge — grabbing kube creds now.
kevin (mlinfra): joining. Noticing 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff in job tp4-train-2026-03.
tina (sre): copying logs from node cg-3-14 and the pod mounts.
ops-bot: log dump endpoint: /var/log/pods/tp4-train/* (attached to bridge)
kevin (mlinfra): logs snippets:
```
I2026-03-17 12:04:22 NCCL WARN Call to cudaDeviceSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
E2026-03-17 12:04:22 NCCL_COLLECTIVE_HANG detected at allreduce, rank 0
CUDA error: Xid 79: device-side assert
OOM when allocating 1.2 GiB for kv-cache
container: tp4-train-worker-7 -> ExitCode: 137 (OOM)
```
raj (eng-ml): Model is a TP4 pipeline-parallel 34B config, seq_len 2048, micro-batch 8 across 4 TP stages. That allocation pattern can spike mem with kv-cache + activations.
maria (infra): Node cg-3-14 shows GPU memory fragmentation and NVLink errors in dmesg; multiple Xid 79 events correlate with pod restarts.
tina (sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain node cg-3-14, 2) scale down tp4 training replicas, 3) enable traffic fallback to single-GPU inference variant.
kevin (mlinfra): Agreed. Also applying quick config to lower micro-batch to 4 for live jobs and enable model-fallback routing for inference traffic.
raj (eng-ml): I'll prepare model rollback to a smaller checkpoint / single-shard inference. Need a 10-15m window to shift pipelines.
maria (infra): Starting drain: `kubectl drain cg-3-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — cordon done, evicting pods now.
ops-bot: customer telemetry: us-west-2 saw 400/503 spikes between 12:03-12:10 UTC; ~7% of routed requests hit fallback, latency increased +30-120ms for those.
tina (sre): Customer impact: degradation for 3 Dedicated enterprise customers in us-west-2; CS notified and incident status updated. No evidence of data exfiltration.
kevin (mlinfra): Live mitigation actions executed: scaled replicas 12->4, applied routing override to fallback model, lowered micro-batch on active jobs. Monitoring error rate and latency.
raj (eng-ml): Applied quantization profile and offloaded some KV-cache to host memory for fallback; watching for accuracy regressions.
maria (infra): Node drain completed. Kubelet restart and driver probe in progress. Kernel logs show driver 535.101 had a regression — scheduling a rolling driver upgrade for suspect hosts.
ops-bot: Actions logged: [evict affected jobs] [apply fallback routing] [reduce micro-batch] [driver follow-up]. Postmortem owner: raj (eng-ml).
kevin (mlinfra): Handing on-call for the incident to raj for deep dive/postmortem. I'll remain on-call for fallback verification until 13:00 UTC.
tina (sre): I'll run stability sweeps for 1 hour and re-run the collective stress test. Page SRE immediately if NCCL errors reappear.
raj (eng-ml): Root-cause hypothesis: NVLink instability combined with GPU driver mismatch causing fragmented allocations and NCCL hang in TP pipeline. Will validate with reproducer.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged and mitigated. Bridge closed at 1767112500. Postmortem ticket INF-2319 created and assigned to raj.

maria (infra): Thanks all — monitoring continues. :thumbsup:
